crime_highlights: Ms. Poitras pleaded guilty to a charge of theft under $5,000 after stealing a shirt (having a value of $25) from a store in Prince George
She has a record of some 36 offences dating from 1996 to this year, most of which are thefts under $5,000
she re-offended again in 2005, receiving a sentence of 90 days on a PSP
rationale_highlights: become addicted to drugs or alcohol and simply pass their lives going in and out of prison
I am also of the view that the offence here did not justify a nine-month sentence, even given Ms. Poitras's record.
note: Court faults failure to consider s. 718.2(e) in para 11 but gives no clear effect.

crime_highlights: Mr. Pratt returned to the driver's seat and suddenly and unexpectedly accelerated away from the gas pump
The car ran over him and Mr. DePatie was caught in the undercarriage of the car.
Mr. Pratt was aware that he had struck someone, but he continued to accelerate away, dragging Mr. DePatie with him.
For 7.5 kilometres he drove while dragging Mr. DePatie along the road beneath him.
Mr. Pratt continued to drive, leaving Mr. DePatie's body on the road to be found by others shortly thereafter.
rationale_highlights: Parliament has said to the courts that they must respond to the needs of aboriginal young persons that come before them, while maintaining a standard of fair and proportionate accountability.
It is a consideration that, if it has any consequence, can only lead to mitigation of sentence, either in duration or as to its terms.

in the case of a young aboriginal person before the courts, as was here the case with Mr. Pratt, and a history of broken family guidance and an absentee parent, as again was here the case, the Act requires greater attention to this circumstance than was accorded by the sentencing judge
note: Youth offender; manslaughter by dragging gas station attendant.

crime_highlights: the appellant stole a bottle of whiskey from a liquor store in a shopping mall in Williams Lake
she returned to the mall and shoplifted some bed sheets
she returned a third time and stole various items of clothing worth $440
rationale_highlights: sets out the appellant's aboriginal background and the many disadvantages and difficulties she has experienced as a result of her upbringing
this information would likely have had an effect on the disposition
The sentencing judge was obviously searching for some alternative to a lengthy term of incarceration for the appellant and found none.
note: Fresh evidence Gladue-type report; court says only it would likely have affected disposition.
